items.title: fastapi-cache-di
items.text:
Speed up FastAPI startup by caching its dependency-tree introspection.

At startup, FastAPI introspects every route's dependency tree — calling get_typed_signature, get_dependant and, up to FastAPI 0.140, get_flat_dependant — with no caching. Dependencies shared across many routes (auth checks, DB handles, role guards …) are re-introspected from scratch for every route. On a large API this dominates import/boot time.

fastapi-cache-di monkeypatches those functions to memoize their results for the duration of route loading, then restores the originals. On FastAPI ≤ 0.140 the heavy one is get_flat_dependant, called once per route in APIRoute.__init__: caching its recursive results turns O(routes × tree-depth) into O(routes + unique-deps). FastAPI 0.141 removed it, so only the other two are cached there.

items.title: Install
items.text:
Install fastapi-cache-di with pip:

pip install fastapi-cache-di

Or add it to your project with uv:

uv add fastapi-cache-di

items.title: Quickstart
items.text:
Wrap the code that loads your routes with the context manager:

from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

from fastapi_cache_di import fastapi_deps_cache

app = FastAPI()
users = APIRouter()
orders = APIRouter()
billing = APIRouter()

with fastapi_deps_cache(warm_up=app):
    # Registering routes introspects each dependency tree; caching is active here.
    app.include_router(users)
    app.include_router(orders)
    app.include_router(billing)
# included routes built, originals restored here; cache memory freed

That is all it takes: introspection results are memoized while routes are being registered, and FastAPI's original functions are restored when the block exits.

See the usage guide for manual patching, sharing and inspecting a cache, thread-safety notes, and the opt-in runtime patches that call loop-safe dependencies on the event loop, skip re-walking the sub-tree of dependencies already cached for a request, and solve each route from a plan compiled once. See how it works for the caching internals, and the API reference for the full public API.

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• Python ≥ 3.12
  • FastAPI ≥ 0.112.4

Note

0.112.4 is the floor: that is when FastAPI started calling get_flat_dependant during route construction, which is the hot path this library caches. Validated in CI up to FastAPI 0.143.1.

items.title: API reference
items.text:
Everything below is exported from the top-level fastapi_cache_di package.

from fastapi_cache_di import (
    DepsCache,
    fastapi_deps_cache,
    is_loop_safe,
    loop_safe,
    patch_fastapi_deps_cache,
    patch_fastapi_resolution_plan,
    patch_fastapi_run_in_threadpool,
    patch_fastapi_solve_dependencies,
    unpatch_fastapi_deps_cache,
    unpatch_fastapi_resolution_plan,
    unpatch_fastapi_run_in_threadpool,
    unpatch_fastapi_solve_dependencies,
)

items.title: fastapi_deps_cache
items.text:
fastapi_deps_cache(
    *,
    deps_cache: DepsCache | bool = True,
    warm_up: FastAPI | APIRouter | None = None,
) -> ContextManager[None]

Context manager that enables dependency caching for the block's duration and restores FastAPI's originals on exit.

Parameters

  • deps_cache:
    • True (default) — use a temporary cache scoped to this context.
    • False — no-op; caching is disabled (warm_up is ignored).
    • a DepsCache instance — use (and populate) a shared cache that survives the block.
  • warm_up: an app or router whose included routers' routes are built when the block exits normally, while the cache is still active. From FastAPI 0.137, FastAPI builds them on the first request through each included router instead, after the cache is gone. Mounted sub-applications are not walked: warm each one in its own nested block. No effect on a FastAPI without fastapi.routing.iter_route_contexts (before 0.137.2).

The context manager only tears down what it installed: because patch_fastapi_deps_cache returns False when caching is already active, a nested block does not unpatch and destroy the still-wanted outer cache.

items.title: patch_fastapi_deps_cache
items.text:
patch_fastapi_deps_cache(deps_cache: DepsCache | None = None) -> bool

Install caching wrappers for get_typed_signature, get_dependant and, on FastAPI ≤ 0.140, get_flat_dependant. Call it once, before the app loads its routes.

Parameters

  • deps_cache: a DepsCache instance to use as backing store. If None (default), a new cache is created internally and cleared on unpatch.

Returns True on the first call, False if already patched. When already patched, passing a different deps_cache is ignored (the existing cache is kept) and a warning is logged.

items.title: unpatch_fastapi_deps_cache
items.text:
unpatch_fastapi_deps_cache() -> bool

Restore the original FastAPI functions and free cache memory. Logs a hit/miss summary of the patched functions at INFO level. An internally-created cache is cleared; a caller-owned cache is left populated (entries and counters) for post-hoc inspection.

Returns True if unpatched, False if not currently patched.

items.title: patch_fastapi_run_in_threadpool
items.text:
patch_fastapi_run_in_threadpool(*, inline_classes: bool = False) -> bool

Call loop-safe sync dependencies directly on the event loop. Replaces fastapi.dependencies.utils.run_in_threadpool, which FastAPI awaits for every sync, non-generator dependency at request time; meant to stay active for the app's lifetime. A callable marked with loop_safe is called inline; everything else still goes through the threadpool. Sync generator dependencies and sync endpoints are not affected.

Parameters

  • inline_classes: treat every class as loop-safe, marked or not. Only enable it when no injected class does I/O, takes a lock or computes heavily in its __init__.

Returns True on the first call, False if already patched. Re-patching with a different inline_classes is ignored and logs a warning.

Raises RuntimeError on a FastAPI version that no longer calls dependencies through that global, rather than silently losing the optimization.

items.title: unpatch_fastapi_run_in_threadpool
items.text:
unpatch_fastapi_run_in_threadpool() -> bool

Restore FastAPI's run_in_threadpool for dependencies.

Returns True if unpatched, False if not currently patched.

items.title: loop_safe
items.text:
loop_safe(obj: T) -> T

Mark a sync function or a class as safe to call on the event loop, by setting its __fastapi_loop_safe__ attribute. Returns obj itself, so Depends(obj) and dependency_overrides[obj] keep working. A loop-safe callable must never block.

items.title: is_loop_safe
items.text:
is_loop_safe(call: Callable[..., Any]) -> bool

True if call itself carries the loop-safe marker. The marker is read from the object's own namespace, never inherited; functools.partial wrappers are unwrapped, and a bound method follows its function's marker.

items.title: patch_fastapi_solve_dependencies
items.text:
patch_fastapi_solve_dependencies() -> bool

Skip re-walking the sub-tree of dependencies already solved for a request. Replaces solve_dependencies in fastapi.dependencies.utils and fastapi.routing; meant to stay active for the app's lifetime, independently of the dependency cache.

Returns True on the first call, False if already patched.

Raises RuntimeError on a FastAPI version that no longer defines solve_dependencies in either module, rather than silently losing the optimization.

items.title: unpatch_fastapi_solve_dependencies
items.text:
unpatch_fastapi_solve_dependencies() -> bool

Restore FastAPI's solve_dependencies in both modules. fastapi.routing keeps the patched function while patch_fastapi_resolution_plan is active.

Returns True if unpatched, False if not currently patched.

items.title: patch_fastapi_resolution_plan
items.text:
patch_fastapi_resolution_plan() -> bool

Solve each route's dependencies from a plan compiled on its first request, and compiled again when dependency_overrides change. Replaces solve_dependencies in fastapi.routing, the root call of HTTP routes, WebSocket routes and route groups; meant to stay active for the app's lifetime, independently of the other patches.

Returns True on the first call, False if already patched.

Raises RuntimeError on a FastAPI version missing a function the plan calls.

items.title: unpatch_fastapi_resolution_plan
items.text:
unpatch_fastapi_resolution_plan() -> bool

Solve routes recursively again, as FastAPI does. fastapi.routing keeps the sub-tree skip while patch_fastapi_solve_dependencies is active.

Returns True if unpatched, False if not currently patched.

items.title: DepsCache
items.text:
DepsCache()

Unified backing store for the three levels of memoized introspection data. The hit/miss counters live on the instance (not on module globals), so a caller-owned cache still exposes its effectiveness after unpatch.

Attributes

Attribute Type Description signatures dict[int, inspect.Signature] get_typed_signature results, keyed by id(call) dependants dict[tuple, Dependant] get_dependant results, keyed by a composite tuple of every argument that affects the produced Dependant flat_dependants dict[tuple, Dependant] get_flat_dependant results, keyed by (id(dependant), parent_oauth_scopes); always empty on FastAPI ≥ 0.141 sig_hits, sig_misses int get_typed_signature cache hits / misses dep_hits, dep_misses int get_dependant cache hits / misses flat_hits, flat_misses int get_flat_dependant cache hits / misses; always 0 on FastAPI ≥ 0.141

Methods

  • keep_alive(*objs: object) -> None — pin objects so their id() stays reserved while they are used as cache keys (guards against id() recycling after garbage collection). Called internally by the wrappers.
  • clear() -> None — drop all cached entries and reset every hit/miss counter.

items.title: __version__
items.text: The installed package version, as a string.

items.title: How it works
items.text: patch_fastapi_deps_cache() replaces up to three functions in fastapi.dependencies.utils (plus the fastapi.routing and fastapi.openapi.utils re-imports) with caching wrappers backed by a DepsCache. unpatch_fastapi_deps_cache() restores the originals.

items.title: The cached functions
items.text:
FastAPI introspects every route's dependency tree at startup with no caching. Shared dependencies (an auth check, a DB handle, a role guard …) are re-introspected from scratch for every route that uses them. The functions on that hot path, and how each is keyed:

Function Cache key Why get_typed_signature id(call) avoid repeated signature parsing get_dependant (id(call), path params, name, use_cache, scope kwargs) avoid redundant tree introspection get_flat_dependant (FastAPI ≤ 0.140) (id(dependant), parent_oauth_scopes) the dominant startup cost on those versions

On FastAPI ≤ 0.140, get_flat_dependant is the dominant cost: FastAPI calls it once per route in APIRoute.__init__ to flatten the dependency tree, recursing through every sub-dependency without caching. Caching the recursive results turns O(routes × tree-depth) into O(routes + unique-deps).

FastAPI 0.141 removed get_flat_dependant: it now flattens the tree with iterative walks that build no Dependant, so only get_typed_signature and get_dependant are cached there.

items.title: Where the patch is applied
items.text:
Each function is patched in every module that holds its own reference:

  • get_typed_signature — patched in fastapi.dependencies.utils only (that is the sole caller).
  • get_dependant — patched in fastapi.dependencies.utils (for the recursive calls) and in fastapi.routing (which imports its own reference).
  • get_flat_dependant — patched in fastapi.dependencies.utils (self-recursive calls), fastapi.openapi.utils and fastapi.routing, but only in the modules that actually define it; the patched modules are remembered and restored on unpatch. Nothing is patched from FastAPI 0.141, where the function no longer exists: no attribute is ever injected into a FastAPI module.

The openapi.utils patch is effectively a no-op: both call sites there pass skip_repeats=True, which the wrapper short-circuits straight to the original without caching. It is installed for symmetry and as a safety net.

items.title: Copy-on-return semantics
items.text:
Some Dependant list fields are mutated by FastAPI after introspection returns (route-level parameterless dependencies inserted during routing, and on FastAPI < 0.121 security_requirements). Handing back the shared cached object would leak one route's mutations into every sibling that reuses the same cached entry.

To stay safe, the wrappers shallow-copy the returned Dependant and give it private copies of the mutated list containers:

  • get_flat_dependant results are shallow-copied on the way out, with private copies of path_params, query_params, header_params, cookie_params, body_params and dependencies.
  • get_dependant copies the mutated fields (dependencies, security_requirements) only for the top-level path-operation dependant (name is None), which FastAPI mutates in place. Named sub-dependants are never mutated and keep their cached identity — that identity is what makes the recursive sub-dependency sharing work.

Only the list containers are private; their elements (ModelField and sub-Dependant objects) remain shared references. Appending to or reordering a returned list is safe; mutating an element in place is not.

items.title: Cache-key subtleties
items.text:
• get_dependant folds in only the path param names, not the literal path string. Two routes with the same param names but different literals (/a/{id} vs /b/{id}) deliberately share one cached Dependant — this is what makes cross-route sharing effective. A consequence is that the shared object's .path reflects whichever route populated it first; FastAPI reads .path only for diagnostics, never for routing, so the staleness is cosmetic.
  • The scope-related keyword arguments of get_dependant and get_flat_dependant changed across FastAPI versions. They are captured generically via **kwargs and folded into the key, so the wrappers stay compatible across the supported FastAPI range.
  • Calls with skip_repeats=True (OpenAPI generation) bypass the cache since they depend on a mutable visited list, and are not a startup bottleneck anyway.

items.title: id() recycling protection
items.text: The signature and dependant caches key on id(call) / id(dependant) — the object's memory address. Python recycles id() after an object is garbage collected, so a short-lived callable could be collected and a later object allocated at the same address, then wrongly served the dead object's cached entry. DepsCache holds a strong reference to every keyed object (via keep_alive) so its address stays reserved for the cache's lifetime.

items.title: Calling loop-safe dependencies inline
items.text:
FastAPI awaits fastapi.dependencies.utils.run_in_threadpool(call, **values) for every sub-dependency that is neither a coroutine nor a generator — the only call site of that module global, from FastAPI 0.112.4 to 0.143.1. patch_fastapi_run_in_threadpool() replaces the global: a callable that is loop-safe (or any class, with inline_classes=True) is called inline, everything else is delegated to the function the global held when patching.

  • Why the global, not Dependant.call — rewriting call into an async factory would change the key FastAPI looks overrides up with and stores values under: an override registered on the original class would no longer be found, and shared sub-dependencies would be built twice once overrides are set. Patching the global leaves the call, the cache key and the override lookup untouched.
  • Overrides — the call the replacement receives is the effective one, after dependency_overrides: an override is judged on its own marker.
  • Not affected — sync generator dependencies go through contextmanager_in_threadpool and sync endpoints through fastapi.routing, so both keep their threadpool hop.
  • Guard — a test fails if FastAPI stops awaiting sync dependencies through the module global.

items.title: Skipping cached sub-trees at request time
items.text:
solve_dependencies loops over a dependant's sub-dependencies, recurses into each one, and only then checks whether the sub-dependency's value is already in the request's dependency_cache. patch_fastapi_solve_dependencies() wraps it: when the caller's sub-dependency is cached, the recursive call returns an empty SolvedDependency straight away. The caller then hits its own cache check and reuses the value, so no FastAPI code is copied.

  • Patch points — fastapi.dependencies.utils.solve_dependencies (the recursion looks this module global up at every call) and fastapi.routing.solve_dependencies (imported by name; HTTP routes, WebSocket routes and route groups), which it shares with the resolution plan (see below). The root call never receives a cache, so it is never skipped.
  • Cache key — it must be the exact key FastAPI stores the value under: a dataclass field before FastAPI 0.121, Dependant.cache_key as a cached_property up to 0.139, and fastapi.dependencies.models._get_cache_key from 0.140, called with the _uses_scopes_cache memo the recursion threads through.
  • The caller's sub-dependency — when dependency_overrides is not empty, FastAPI rebuilds every sub-dependant, overridden or not, before recursing. The rebuilt dependant always has use_cache=True and drops its own Security scopes, so its key may not be the one the caller checks. The wrapper therefore tests the caller's own sub-dependant: before delegating, it publishes the dependant's sub-dependants in a ContextVar, and each recursive call takes the next one, since FastAPI recurses exactly once per sub-dependant, in order. A sub-dependant whose name or (overridden) call does not match what the recursive call received is never skipped. The ContextVar is per asyncio task, so concurrent requests never share it.
  • Guards — tests fail if FastAPI stops resolving the recursion through the module global, changes the fields of SolvedDependency, keys its request cache differently, or stops recursing once per sub-dependant in order.

items.title: Solving routes from a precompiled plan
items.text:
patch_fastapi_resolution_plan() replaces the recursion itself. fastapi_cache_di.plan.compile_plan flattens a route's dependency tree into frames (a dependant whose own parameters are extracted after its sub-dependencies) and steps (one per occurrence of a sub-dependency), in FastAPI's evaluation order: depth first, sub-dependencies in the order of dependant.dependencies. Each step carries, precomputed, its request cache key, the kind of its callable (coroutine, sync, sync or async generator), its stack scope, and each frame its non-empty parameter fields, special parameters (Request, WebSocket, HTTPConnection, Response, BackgroundTasks, SecurityScopes) and OAuth scopes. At request time, the plan runs the steps in a single loop.

  • Patch point — fastapi.routing.solve_dependencies, the root call. One dispatcher owns it while either the plan or the sub-tree skip is active: it runs the plan when the plan is active, and the current fastapi.dependencies.utils.solve_dependencies (the skip wrapper or FastAPI) otherwise. The first patch saves FastAPI's original, the last unpatch restores it, in any order. Dependant.call is never rewritten, so the override lookup and the cache keys stay FastAPI's.
  • FastAPI helpers — the functions the plan calls (request_params_to_args, request_body_to_args, run_in_threadpool, the generator helper, solve_dependencies) are looked up on fastapi.dependencies.utils at call time, as FastAPI does, so patch_fastapi_run_in_threadpool() still applies.
  • Repeated occurrences — a repeated occurrence of a use_cache=True dependency is a step that reads the request cache. Its value is missing only when its first occurrence failed validation; FastAPI then solves it again and reports its errors once more, so the step hands that sub-tree to fastapi.dependencies.utils.solve_dependencies, which duplicates the errors exactly like FastAPI.
  • Overrides — the plan is compiled with dependency_overrides applied, rebuilding every sub-dependant with get_dependant like FastAPI, with the scope arguments of each version. The snapshot of the overrides (pairs compared by identity) is checked at every request, immediately when the dict is empty. The rebuilt sub-trees are not kept: frames and steps only keep the values they read, and a repeated occurrence keeps the get_dependant arguments to rebuild its dependant on the error path only.
  • Storage — Dependant cannot carry the plan: from FastAPI 0.140 it is a slotted dataclass, without room for an extra attribute nor weak references. The plans are stored on the route's dependency_overrides_provider (the app), keyed by id() of the root dependant with a strong reference to it (the same protection as id() recycling protection), so they are freed with the app. A root call without a provider is solved by FastAPI.
  • Versions — differences between FastAPI versions are confined to a few adapters chosen from the fields of Dependant and the functions FastAPI defines: the cache key, the OAuth scopes, the callable kind, the exit stacks (per scope from 0.121) and the get_dependant scope arguments.
  • Guards — an equivalence test compares the plan with FastAPI on a reference tree (values, errors, request cache, call and exit order) on every version of the compatibility matrix, and a benchmark gate requires the plan to be at least twice as fast as the sub-tree skip on a tree of 100 dependencies and 211 edges.

items.title: Usage
items.text:
The dependency cache is a startup-only optimization. The cache must be active while FastAPI introspects your routes' dependency trees — that is, while routers are being included / routes registered — and torn down afterwards.

There are three ways to drive it: the context manager, manual patch/unpatch, and a caller-owned shared cache you can inspect afterwards.

Separately, three opt-in runtime patches cut per-request costs, see Calling loop-safe dependencies inline, Skipping the sub-tree of cached dependencies and Solving routes from a precompiled plan.

items.title: Context manager (recommended)
items.text:
fastapi_deps_cache enables caching for the duration of the block, then restores FastAPI's originals and frees the cache memory on exit:

from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

from fastapi_cache_di import fastapi_deps_cache

app = FastAPI()
users = APIRouter()
orders = APIRouter()

with fastapi_deps_cache(warm_up=app):
    app.include_router(users)
    app.include_router(orders)
# included routes built, originals restored here; cache memory freed

The deps_cache keyword controls the backing store:

  • True (default) — use a temporary cache scoped to this context.
  • False — no-op; caching is disabled (handy behind a feature flag).
  • a DepsCache instance — use (and populate) a shared cache that survives the block, see Sharing and inspecting the cache.
# Disable caching without changing the call site.
with fastapi_deps_cache(deps_cache=False):
    app.include_router(users)

items.title: Warming up included routers
items.text:
From FastAPI 0.137, include_router no longer copies the included routes into the app: it adds a wrapper, and FastAPI builds the effective routes on the first request through each included router (or the first /openapi.json). That build introspects every dependency tree again, after the block has exited and without the cache, so the first request is as slow as without the library.

warm_up takes the app (or an APIRouter) whose included routes are built when the block exits normally, while the cache is still active:

with fastapi_deps_cache(warm_up=app):
    app.include_router(users)
  • It relies on fastapi.routing.iter_route_contexts, and has no effect on a FastAPI that lacks it (before 0.137.2). Before 0.137, nothing is deferred.
  • It does not run when the block raises; the exception propagates unchanged.
  • Routes added after the block, routes of mounted sub-applications (app.mount(...)) and frontend() routes are still built on first use, without the cache: warm a mounted FastAPI app with its own nested fastapi_deps_cache(warm_up=subapp) block.
  • It is ignored with deps_cache=False.
  • Nested in another block, or under an active patch_fastapi_deps_cache(), it runs with that cache.

Note

The context manager is safe to nest. patch_fastapi_deps_cache is a no-op when caching is already active, so an inner block never tears down the still-wanted outer cache — only the block that actually installed the patch unpatches on exit.

items.title: Manual patch / unpatch
items.text:
When your route loading is not expressible as a single block, patch before any routes are loaded and unpatch in a finally:

from fastapi import FastAPI

from fastapi_cache_di import patch_fastapi_deps_cache, unpatch_fastapi_deps_cache


def load_all_routes(app: FastAPI) -> None:
    """Register the application's routers (introspection happens here)."""


app = FastAPI()

patch_fastapi_deps_cache()  # call before any routes are loaded
try:
    load_all_routes(app)
finally:
    unpatch_fastapi_deps_cache()  # logs hit/miss stats, restores originals

patch_fastapi_deps_cache() returns True on the first call and False if caching is already active. unpatch_fastapi_deps_cache() returns True if it restored the originals and False if nothing was patched. On unpatch, a summary of the hit/miss counters is logged at INFO level under the fastapi_cache_di.patch logger.

items.title: Sharing and inspecting the cache
items.text:
Pass your own DepsCache to keep the memoized data and the hit/miss counters after the context exits — a caller-owned cache is not cleared on unpatch, so you can measure how effective the caching was:

from fastapi import FastAPI

from fastapi_cache_di import DepsCache, fastapi_deps_cache


def load_all_routes(app: FastAPI) -> None:
    """Register the application's routers (introspection happens here)."""


app = FastAPI()
cache = DepsCache()

with fastapi_deps_cache(deps_cache=cache):
    load_all_routes(app)

# The cache survives the context, so you can inspect what was memoized
# and how effective it was (hit/miss counters live on the instance).
print(len(cache.dependants), len(cache.flat_dependants))
print(cache.flat_hits, cache.flat_misses)

DepsCache exposes three memoization stores and a hit/miss counter pair for each:

Store Counters Populated from signatures sig_hits, sig_misses get_typed_signature dependants dep_hits, dep_misses get_dependant flat_dependants flat_hits, flat_misses get_flat_dependant (FastAPI ≤ 0.140; empty from 0.141)

Call cache.clear() to drop all entries and reset every counter, so the same instance can be reused for another loading pass.

items.title: Thread-safety
items.text:
Warning

All patch state is process-global and patching swaps FastAPI module attributes for the whole process. It is not re-entrant across threads: call patch/unpatch (or the context manager) from a single thread, during startup only.

Because the counters live on the DepsCache instance rather than on module globals, a caller-owned cache still exposes its statistics after unpatch.

Calling patch_fastapi_deps_cache(deps_cache=...) while a patch is already active keeps the existing cache and logs a warning — the new cache is ignored until you unpatch first.

items.title: Calling loop-safe dependencies inline
items.text:
At request time, FastAPI calls every dependency that is neither a coroutine nor a generator through the threadpool: every Depends(SomeClass) and every plain def dependency costs a round trip to a worker thread, often far more than a class whose __init__ only stores its arguments.

patch_fastapi_run_in_threadpool() lets such dependencies run directly on the event loop. It is opt-in, because the library cannot tell whether a call blocks:

  • loop_safe marks one sync function or class (it returns the same object, so Depends(...) and dependency_overrides keep working);
  • inline_classes=True treats every class as loop-safe;
  • everything else still goes through the threadpool, as do sync generator dependencies and sync endpoints.
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI

from fastapi_cache_di import loop_safe, patch_fastapi_run_in_threadpool

patch_fastapi_run_in_threadpool(inline_classes=True)


@loop_safe
def get_tenant_id() -> str:
    return "acme"


class UserRepository:
    def __init__(self, tenant_id: Annotated[str, Depends(get_tenant_id)]) -> None:
        self.tenant_id = tenant_id


app = FastAPI()


@app.get("/users")
async def list_users(repo: Annotated[UserRepository, Depends()]) -> str:
    return repo.tenant_id

Unlike the dependency cache, this patch stays active for the app's lifetime; unpatch_fastapi_run_in_threadpool() restores FastAPI's behavior. The patches of this library are independent: any of them can be used without the others.

Warning

A loop-safe callable must never block: no I/O, no lock, no heavy computation. A blocking call on the event loop stalls every in-flight request. A JWT dependency that fetches its signing keys over HTTP when they are not cached, for instance, must stay in the threadpool. The marker is never inherited: a subclass of a marked class must be marked on its own.

An override in dependency_overrides is judged on its own marker, not on the original's: an unmarked override (a test lambda, for instance) goes through the threadpool.

The marker is the __fastapi_loop_safe__ attribute, a contract shared with fastapi-standalone-di: an object marked by either library's loop_safe is recognised by both, without one depending on the other.

items.title: Skipping the sub-tree of cached dependencies
items.text:
At request time, FastAPI solves the whole sub-tree of a dependency before checking whether its value is already in the request's cache. The cache saves the call, not the walk: a dependency shared across a deep tree (a DB handle, a session service, repositories …) has its sub-tree solved again at every occurrence, query, header and cookie parameters included, and the result is thrown away. The cost grows with the number of occurrences in the tree, not with the number of unique dependencies.

patch_fastapi_solve_dependencies() stops that walk as soon as the value is cached; FastAPI then reuses the cached value as before. Unlike the dependency cache, it is meant to stay active for the app's lifetime:

from fastapi import FastAPI

from fastapi_cache_di import patch_fastapi_solve_dependencies

patch_fastapi_solve_dependencies()

app = FastAPI()

unpatch_fastapi_solve_dependencies() restores FastAPI's behavior.

The values injected into endpoints are unchanged. The only visible difference: a use_cache=False dependency nested under a cached dependency is no longer called again during the skipped walk, whose result was discarded anyway. It works the same with dependency_overrides set, as in most test suites.

items.title: Solving routes from a precompiled plan
items.text:
Even with the sub-tree skip, FastAPI still walks the dependency tree recursively at every request, and recomputes for each dependency what only depends on the route: its cache key, whether it is a coroutine, a generator or a plain function, which request parameters it reads. On routes with about a hundred dependencies, that framework work outweighs the dependencies themselves.

patch_fastapi_resolution_plan() compiles each route's dependency tree once, at the route's first request, into a flat plan in FastAPI's evaluation order, then solves every request of that route from the plan in a single loop. On a route of 100 dependencies and 211 edges, solving a request takes about a tenth of the time it takes with the sub-tree skip alone. It is opt-in, and stays active for the app's lifetime; unpatch_fastapi_resolution_plan() restores FastAPI's recursive walk.

from fastapi import FastAPI

from fastapi_cache_di import patch_fastapi_resolution_plan

patch_fastapi_resolution_plan()

app = FastAPI()

The values injected into endpoints, the validation errors (including the ones a dependency reports at each of its occurrences), the request's dependency cache and the exit order of yield dependencies are the ones FastAPI produces. Like the sub-tree skip, a use_cache=False dependency nested under an already solved dependency is not called again.

  • Overrides — the plan is compiled with dependency_overrides applied, and compiled again when they change, so a test suite that sets overrides is solved by the plan too. A route keeps one plan without overrides and one for the last overrides it saw. A plan only keeps what it reads at request time, not the sub-trees FastAPI rebuilds under overrides: a few tens of KiB for a route of 100 dependencies, with or without overrides.
  • Storage — a route's plans are stored on its app and freed with it. A dependency tree changed after the route's first request is not compiled again.
  • Combining — it is independent of the other patches. Combined with patch_fastapi_solve_dependencies(), either can be removed first; the plan takes over while both are active. Sync dependencies still go through patch_fastapi_run_in_threadpool() when it is active.

Warning

The plan reproduces FastAPI internals (solve_dependencies, its request cache keys and its evaluation order). The test suite compares the plan with FastAPI on a reference dependency tree for every FastAPI version of the compatibility matrix, and a benchmark gate fails the pipeline if the plan stops being at least twice as fast as the sub-tree skip. The patch raises a RuntimeError on a FastAPI version that no longer defines a function the plan calls.
